final_recommendation: The room converged on a bifurcated nearshoring model with a 50% relocation-signal trigger to flip from Scenario A (domestic wage-floor compliance) to Scenario B (Mexico relocation absorption). Pre-pay settles before PO commitment for three high-risk tiers (electronics, harness, stamped-metal), killing receivables risk; compliance remediation reserve ($600–800K) covers mandatory first-article inspection on nearshore intake; Friday data pull locks supplier relocation signals to operationalize the trigger.
minority_objections: Trade credit underwriter initially pushed to separate receivables risk from pre-pay coverage, but was overruled when CFO locked pre-pay timing before PO commitment
Supplier initially resisted absorbing dual default risk (nearshore + domestic stayers) under a single reserve, but accepted the split after CFO clarified the $800K reserve covers both cohorts
key_conflicts: Circular dependency in R2: auto_strategy demanded supplier matrix, supplier demanded CFO pre-pay decision, CFO demanded supply-chain timeline—resolved when CFO unilaterally locked pre-pay before PO
R4–R5: Five specialists surfaced that Tier 2/3 relocation splits into multiple risk profiles; CFO's attempt to force a single baseline was denied, leading to the bifurcated Scenario A/B model

R6: Compliance and supplier clashed on whether 50% trigger accelerates certification audit timing or just flips pricing—resolved when compliance clarified CBP audit clock doesn't shift but sampling intensity spikes
key_concessions: CFO conceded that pre-pay covers tooling capex but NOT compliance remediation, creating a separate $200–400K/tier exposure line
Auto_strategy conceded that Tier 2/3 shops outside pre-pay are left to self-fund or relocate, absorbing supplier churn as baseline cost
Political risk insurer conceded to price Scenario B (relocation absorption) as baseline despite lack of hard relocation data, accepting Friday data pull as sufficient
Compliance conceded that intake certification gaps (5–15% penalties) are a separate, lower-priority risk layer than labor-content audit failures (20–25%)
red_lines: Pre-pay must settle BEFORE PO commitment (locked by CFO in R2)—no receivables window tolerated
50% relocation-signal threshold triggers automatic flip to Scenario B repricing (locked by CFO in R6)
Friday data pull on Tier 2/3 relocation signals is non-negotiable for operationalizing the trigger (locked by supply_chain_consultant in R5–R6)
Compliance remediation reserve must be separate from pre-pay tooling capex (locked by compliance_lawyer in R2–R3)
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Business interruption exposure from model-level holds if CBP flags first-batch labor docs—mentioned by auto_strategy in R4 but never priced or operationalized

Contingent business interruption from upstream Tier 3 supplier defaults—trade_credit_underwriter raised receivables risk in R2–R4 but it was killed by pre-pay timing, leaving downstream exposure unaddressed
2026 USMCA review shock layer—mentioned by supply_chain_consultant in R5 as a forward political risk but never translated into a concrete insurance variable or trigger
Production schedule lock discipline—supplier flagged in R3 that locking labor docs without locking production specs creates wage-compliance drift, but no enforcement mechanism was priced
downstream_risk_variables: Nearshore intake certification gap: 5–15% civil penalty on landed value, auditable within 30 days of entry
Labor-content audit failure: 20–25% penalty if non-compliance found 60–120 days post-shipment
Compliance remediation reserve: $600–800K for mandatory first-article inspection if 50%+ of cohort relocates in compressed window
Supplier insolvency window: 60–90 days for Tier 2 electronics/harness shops if nearshoring forced without subsidy
Pre-pay capex bucket: locked for three tiers (electronics, harness, stamped-metal), settles 5 days before PO commitment
50% relocation-signal trigger: automatic flip from Scenario A (domestic compliance) to Scenario B (Mexico relocation absorption)
CBP audit sampling intensity: spikes to mandatory first-article inspection when nearshore intake volume jumps in 45-day window
uncertainty_notes: The room has no hard data yet on which Tier 2/3 shops are actually relocating versus self-funding wage-floor compliance—Friday data pull is the critical dependency. The $800K compliance remediation reserve assumes both nearshore mandatory inspection AND domestic stayer defaults, but the split between those two cohorts remains unquantified. The 2026 USMCA review was flagged as a forward shock layer but never operationalized into a concrete political-risk trigger or premium adjustment.
